newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Mazarin seen among favourites in Uzbek gold tender.
newsitem.headline: Mazarin seen among favourites in Uzbek gold tender.

text.p: Canada's Mazarin Mining Corp appears to be among the front-runners in the race for rights to develop prize gold deposits in the former Soviet republic of Uzbekistan, an official source said on Wednesday.
The source in the State Committee for Geological and Mineral Resources said the committee was in talks with Mazarin to carry out geological surveys on the reserves.

The tender is for seven gold deposits in the Kyzylkum and Nuratinskiye mountains with total estimated reserves of 1,720 tonnes. It was originally announced in June last year, but the results have been postponed several times since then.
A second committee source said the tender would probably be announced by the end of the month.
"The tender is not completed. The winner has already been chosen, but the results will be officially announced in the second half of June," he said.
The second source declined to comment on whether Mazarin was likely to be the eventual winner of the tender, adding it was still possible that a group of companies could be named winners.
He said the committee could give no further information on the tender until details of the deal had been agreed among the parties involved.

According to the rules of the tender, the winner would set up a joint venture with the committee to produce gold if its geological surveys showed there was enough gold to make industrial production profitable.
The most promising of the seven deposits are the Dzhetymtauskaya and Karamurunskaya fields with estimated reserves of 400 and 250 tonnes of gold respectively.
The Karamurunskaya field also has estimated copper reserves of 2.5 million tonnes.
Around 17 companies originally took part in the tender, including RTZ Corporation Plc and Nelson Gold Corp Ltd of Canada, BHP and WMC Ltd of Australia and Mitsubishi Corp and Marubeni Corp of Japan.
